LESSON: THE BUILT ENVIRONMENTS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 1.5: The Built Environments
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The Built Environments, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we conserve the historic built environments?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Built Environments together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Love: Learners portray a caring attitude as they participate in conservation activities for historic built environments within the locality.

● Peace: Learners display tolerance as they brainstorm the main historic built environments in Kenya.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental Education: Learners participate in conservation activities for historic built environments within the locality.

Link to other learning areas:

● Learners will apply care for environment skills as they participate in conservation of historic built environments within the locality.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Resource persons, maps, tactile maps, digital resources with assistive technology, charts, marker pens, approved text books and other

printed resources or braille resources.
